title: Add information about removable settings to the deprecation info API

timeline.message: Providing information about which settings can be dynamically removed (work in progress)
timeline.author: Keith Massey

timeline.author: Keith Massey

timeline.body:
Deprecated settings that are only set dynamically (i.e. not in elasticsearch.yml) could also be removed dynamically. This
PR adds information about these settings to the deprecation info API.
Closes #83116

timeline.author: Keith Massey
Keith Massey

timeline.body: Converted to a draft because I realized a shortcoming -- if a property is in elasticsearch.yml on one node but not on another (and it's also set as a dynamic setting), you'll get two separate DeprecationIssues in the response -- one saying you can fix it dynamically and one not saying that.

timeline.message: Deduplicating issues that differ only by removable settings
timeline.author: Keith Massey

timeline.body: This function feels really large, could you split it up into smaller pieces? Maybe a separate part for retrieving the leastCommonRemovableSettings?

I think it's kind of hard to follow the logic for when a setting is removable, perhaps we can bump this up to the `DeprecationIssue` level? (even if it's not a class variable, but computed on a method like `hasRemovableSettings()`

I think all these map comparisons have convinced me that it would be better to make `RemovalAction` an actual class and a class variable on the `DeprecationIssue` class, and then add methods to interact with those actions directly. It's hard for me to follow the logic entirely through here with all the `Map<String, Object>` around (and also, those make me concerned when it comes to type-safety)

Thanks for working on this Keith, I tried looking at this multiple times, but each time I found it hard to follow the entire logic through (not your fault, just because of the generic maps all over).

What do you think of my suggestion to make the actions and settings removal action first-class objects? I think it might make it easier to read through the flow of the code.

timeline.body: Seems like this could be `similarIssues.get(0)` since it's not filtering or anything?

reply.body: Yeah that's what I originally had it as, but I changed it to make it clear that it could be any (the first one's not special). I can put it back. I flip-flopped a couple of times on this and am not tied to either way.

timeline.body: I think this can be `private` since it's only used from this same file

Do we need the `UnknownAction` at all, or can we be strict and throw an exception if it's not in the format we expect? Do you think that would be too strict here? (especially since this `_meta` map the user has no control over, so I think we'd only be limiting plugins)

reply.body: Yeah I was afraid I'd break some plugin that I don't know about. If you're certain that no one else is putting in any other `action`s, I can remove this.

timeline.body:
I think this LGTM, I left three pretty minor comments.

I do think we incur a bit of tech debt for this, but since it's 7.17 I think it's reasonable (tell me if you disagree!). I think that we will need to plan for this with whatever code we want to do this behavior with in the 8.x line.

> I think this LGTM, I left three pretty minor comments.
> 
> I do think we incur a bit of tech debt for this, but since it's 7.17 I think it's reasonable (tell me if you disagree!). I think that we will need to plan for this with whatever code we want to do this behavior with in the 8.x line.

Oh there's definitely new tech debt here due to the fact that `meta` is just a map of string to object, and that we're having to layer in meaning. I agree that it's fine for now, and better than the alternative of a major overhaul in 7.x. As we've discussed, we need to change `meta` into something more concrete in 8.x.
